name: LEGACY / LOCAL EXPERIMENTATION — Ajoop n8n bridge (NOT the public Ajoop request path)

meta.description: LEGACY / LOCAL EXPERIMENTATION — NOT THE PUBLIC AJOOP REQUEST PATH. Ajoop 5.0 moved the public path to server/ajoop-bridge.mjs (browser -> HTTPS edge -> 127.0.0.1:8787 Node bridge -> 127.0.0.1:11434 Ollama). This workflow is retained only for local experimentation and is not wired to the site. It was retired from the public path because n8n execution history retained visitor questions even with every documented save flag set to none/false; the Node bridge stores nothing. See docs/ajoop-local-ai.md.

environment_variables_required.AJOOP_AI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call this bridge, e.g. "https://kaanbalci.com,http://localhost:4173". Never "*": this endpoint runs on a personal machine.
environment_variables_required.OLLAMA_BASE_URL: Local Ollama base URL. Default http://127.0.0.1:11434 — loopback only, never a public bind address.
environment_variables_required.AJOOP_AI_MODEL: Ollama model tag to use, e.g. qwen3:4b.
environment_variables_required.AJOOP_AI_MAX_QUESTION_CHARS: Maximum accepted question length, e.g. 500. Requests above this are rejected before any inference runs.
environment_variables_required.N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE: Must be "false". This template is configured entirely through environment variables, and n8n blocks $env inside nodes by default. With the default, the Code nodes see no configuration and the Ollama nodes cannot resolve their URL, so every request degrades to a rejection.

nodes.name: Ajoop Webhook
nodes.notes: POST only. allowedOrigins is a literal on purpose: the Webhook node resolves parameters outside a Code node, and n8n blocks $env there by default, which made the workflow fail to start with HTTP 500. It governs CORS/preflight headers only — the authoritative origin check is in Validate Request, driven by AJOOP_AI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. Edit this list when the site's origins change.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $env.AJOOP_AI_MODEL || 'qwen3:4b', stream: false, think: true, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: $json.system }, { role: 'user', content: $json.user } ], options: { temperature: 0.1, top_p: 0.9, num_predict: 1024, num_ctx: 4096 } }) }}

nodes.name: Ollama Chat
nodes.notes: Loopback only. think:true is load-bearing: with think:false this model streams untagged chain-of-thought straight into message.content, so ENABLING thinking is what keeps it out of the answer (Ollama returns it separately in message.thinking, which is discarded). Measured on an RTX 4050 with qwen3:4b fully GPU-resident: 9-21s per request. Raising num_predict above 1024 does not improve reliability — the model often stops of its own accord after thinking without emitting content, which the output validator turns into a clean fallback. See docs/ajoop-local-ai.md for the model-reliability finding.

nodes.name: Ollama Health
nodes.notes: Loopback model inventory. Health is available only when Ollama responds and the configured model is installed.

nodes.name: Respond to Ajoop
nodes.notes: Always HTTP 200 with an ok flag. The browser treats ok:false exactly like a network failure and shows its deterministic answer.
